figures.title: Warm success and fresh-start verification cross different boundaries
figures.desc: A three-part comparison separates temporary warm cargo, the declared cold reset, and durable workstation state that must still produce new evidence.
figures.caption: Read left to right: remove only the help the readiness claim should not need, then require durable state to generate a new artifact.
figures.transcript: Warm cargo includes open processes, session-only variables, a remembered working folder, running services, cached screens, and old smoke files. The fresh-start boundary closes relevant processes, restarts the machine when safe, opens a fresh shell and apps, and moves old outputs out of the smoke folder. Durable state includes installed tools, saved user or machine settings, intended credential state, and written instructions. A fresh-start pass occurs only when that durable state generates new smoke files after the boundary; the old warm result belongs to the earlier activity.

items.label: FRESH-START BOUNDARY
items.detail: Restart · new shell · empty smoke folder

figures.title: Fresh-start verification in five moves
figures.desc: A five-stage flow removes temporary setup help, checks durable configuration, and regenerates the expected smoke files.
figures.caption: Move old output aside, cross the fresh-start boundary, and require each tool to create its file again.
figures.transcript: First, finish the normal three-tool verification. Second, move old smoke files aside so they cannot stand in for a new result. Third, restart safely and open a new shell and newly opened apps. Fourth, run the current key, version, and tool checks and inspect each newly appearing file. Fifth, continue when all three files are correct, return to the affected setup step for warm-state problems, or bring external and policy blockers to the install clinic.

figures.title: Hidden-state diagnosis surface
figures.desc: A matrix maps five warm-state clues to their cold observations and the durable promotion or handoff each observation requires.
figures.caption: Find the warm clue in the first column, inspect the cold result, then either promote the missing state into the written setup or hand it to its owner.
figures.transcript: For process environment, a warm-only variable becomes absent after reset, so save it through the approved user or machine path and retest. For an open app or inherited folder, reopening lands elsewhere, so record the project and working location in the procedure. For prior evidence, an old file survives without a new activity, so isolate old output and require a post-boundary artifact. For external service state, local setup reaches a quota, ACL, network, or provider boundary, so record the blocker and hand it to the responsible owner rather than reinstalling. For human memory, a second operator stalls without coaching, so promote the missing launch or decision step into the written path and repeat the transfer.
